Ace Campus course data

This file feeds the Ace Campus portal. 12 courses live, 8 on the plan. Every numerical answer was checked in code (SymPy) when this file was built.

Calculus I (135 questions)

  • Functions and limits: Functions, domains and inverses, Limits and the limit laws, One-sided limits, infinite limits and asymptotes, Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem
  • The derivative: The derivative as a limit, Power, constant and sum rules, Product and quotient rules, The chain rule
  • More derivatives: Derivatives of trigonometric functions, Exponential and logarithmic derivatives, Implicit differentiation, Related rates
  • Applications of the derivative: Critical points and extreme values, The Mean Value Theorem and the shape of a graph, Optimisation, L'Hôpital's rule and linear approximation
  • Integration: Antiderivatives and indefinite integrals, Riemann sums and the definite integral, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Integration by substitution, Area between curves

Linear Algebra (114 questions)

  • Systems of linear equations: Linear systems and their solutions, Gaussian elimination, Reduced row echelon form and rank, Homogeneous systems and parametric solutions
  • Matrix algebra: Matrix operations, Transpose and special matrices, The inverse of a matrix, Matrix equations and invertibility
  • Determinants: Computing determinants, Properties of determinants, Cramer's rule, area and volume
  • Vectors and vector spaces: Vectors, dot product, length and angle, Span and linear independence, Subspaces, basis and dimension, Null space, column space and rank–nullity
  • Linear transformations and eigenvalues: Linear transformations and their matrices, Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, Diagonalisation, Orthogonality and projections

Probability and Statistics (120 questions)

  • Describing data: Types of data and sampling, Measures of centre, Measures of spread, Shape, box plots and outliers
  • Probability: Sample spaces and the rules of probability, Conditional probability and independence, Bayes' theorem, Counting: permutations and combinations
  • Random variables and distributions: Discrete random variables: expectation and variance, The binomial distribution, The Poisson distribution, Continuous random variables
  • Normal distribution, sampling and confidence intervals: The normal distribution and z-scores, Sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem, Confidence intervals for a mean, Confidence intervals for a proportion
  • Hypothesis testing and regression: Hypothesis testing: p-values and errors, Tests for a mean and a proportion, The chi-square test of independence, Correlation and linear regression

Calculus II (120 questions)

  • Techniques of integration: Integration by parts, Trigonometric integrals, Trigonometric substitution, Partial fractions
  • Volumes, arc length and improper integrals: Volumes by discs and washers, Volumes by cylindrical shells, Arc length and surface area, Improper integrals
  • Sequences and series: Sequences and their limits, Series: geometric, telescoping and the divergence test, The integral and comparison tests, The ratio test and alternating series
  • Power series and Taylor series: Power series and radius of convergence, Taylor and Maclaurin series, Taylor polynomials and the error bound, Differentiating and integrating power series
  • Differential equations, parametric curves and polar coordinates: Separable differential equations, First-order linear equations, Parametric curves, Polar coordinates

Principles of Microeconomics (120 questions)

  • Scarcity, demand and supply: Scarcity, opportunity cost and the PPF, Demand, Supply, Market equilibrium and change
  • Elasticity and government intervention: Price elasticity of demand, Income, cross-price and supply elasticity, Price ceilings and price floors, Taxes, subsidies and their incidence
  • Consumers, producers and costs: Consumer and producer surplus, Utility and consumer choice, Production and short-run costs, Long-run costs and economies of scale
  • Market structures: Perfect competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic competition, Oligopoly and game theory
  • Factor markets and market failure: Labour markets and wages, Externalities, Public goods and common resources, Asymmetric information

Principles of Macroeconomics (120 questions)

  • Measuring the economy: GDP and how it is measured, Real GDP and economic growth, Inflation and price indices, Unemployment
  • Aggregate demand and aggregate supply: Consumption, saving and the multiplier, Aggregate demand, Aggregate supply, Macroeconomic equilibrium and shocks
  • Money, banking and monetary policy: Money and its functions, Banks and money creation, Central banks and monetary policy, The quantity theory of money and inflation
  • Fiscal policy and public debt: The government budget, Fiscal policy and its multipliers, Automatic stabilisers and crowding out, Public debt and its sustainability
  • Growth and the open economy: Long-run economic growth, International trade and protection, Exchange rates, The balance of payments

Financial Accounting I (120 questions)

  • The accounting framework: The accounting equation, Double-entry bookkeeping, The trial balance, Accounting concepts and principles
  • Period-end adjustments: Accruals and prepayments, Depreciation of non-current assets, Inventory valuation, Irrecoverable debts and allowances
  • Financial statements and the bank: The income statement, The statement of financial position, The statement of cash flows, Bank reconciliation
  • Interpreting financial statements: Profitability ratios, Liquidity ratios, Efficiency (working capital) ratios, Gearing and investor ratios
  • Control accounts, errors, partnerships and companies: Control accounts, Correcting errors and the suspense account, Partnership accounts, Limited company accounts

Programming with Python (120 questions)

  • Python basics: Variables, types and expressions, Input, output and strings, Making decisions with if, Repeating with loops
  • Data structures: Lists, Tuples and dictionaries, Sets, Comprehensions and nested data
  • Functions, modules and errors: Defining and calling functions, Scope, default arguments and recursion, Modules and the standard library, Errors and exceptions
  • Files, objects and testing: Reading and writing files, Classes and objects, Inheritance and polymorphism, Testing and debugging
  • Algorithms and working with data: Searching algorithms, Sorting algorithms, Algorithm efficiency and Big O, Processing data with Python

General Chemistry (120 questions)

  • Atoms, moles and stoichiometry: Atomic structure and isotopes, The mole and molar mass, Balanced equations and stoichiometry, Solutions and concentration
  • Electrons, bonding and molecular shape: Electron configuration and periodic trends, Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, Molecular shape and polarity, Intermolecular forces and physical properties
  • Gases and thermochemistry: The gas laws, The ideal gas equation, Enthalpy changes and Hess's law, Calorimetry and bond enthalpies
  • Rates, equilibrium, acids and bases: Reaction rates and rate laws, Chemical equilibrium and Kc, Le Chatelier's principle, Acids, bases and pH
  • Thermodynamics, redox and organic chemistry: Entropy and Gibbs free energy, Redox and oxidation numbers, Electrochemical cells, Introduction to organic chemistry

Physics I: Mechanics (120 questions)

  • Describing motion (kinematics): Units, dimensions and vectors, Motion in one dimension, Projectile motion, Uniform circular motion
  • Forces and Newton's laws: Newton's laws of motion, Weight, normal force, tension and friction, Inclined planes and connected objects, Forces in circular motion
  • Work, energy and power: Work and kinetic energy, Potential energy and conservation of energy, Power and efficiency, Springs and elastic energy
  • Momentum and collisions: Momentum and impulse, Conservation of momentum, Elastic and inelastic collisions, Explosions, recoil and centre of mass
  • Rotation, gravitation and oscillations: Torque and equilibrium, Rotational dynamics and angular momentum, Gravitation and orbits, Simple harmonic motion

Cell Biology (120 questions)

  • The molecules of life: Water, pH and the chemistry of life, Carbohydrates and lipids, Proteins, Nucleic acids
  • Cell structure: Cell theory and microscopy, Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, Organelles and the endomembrane system, The cytoskeleton, cell walls and junctions
  • Membranes, transport and signalling: Membrane structure, Diffusion and osmosis, Active transport and bulk transport, Cell signalling
  • Cell energetics: Energy, ATP and enzymes, Glycolysis, the link reaction and the Krebs cycle, Oxidative phosphorylation and fermentation, Photosynthesis
  • The cell cycle and gene expression: The cell cycle and mitosis, Meiosis and genetic variation, DNA replication, Gene expression: transcription and translation

Introduction to Psychology (120 questions)

  • Psychology as a science: History and perspectives of psychology, Research methods, Descriptive statistics and correlation, Research ethics
  • Biological bases of behaviour: Neurons and neurotransmission, The nervous system and the brain, Sensation and perception, Consciousness and sleep
  • Learning, memory and cognition: Classical conditioning, Operant and observational learning, Memory, Thinking, language and intelligence
  • Development, motivation and personality: Lifespan development, Motivation and emotion, Personality, Stress, coping and health
  • Social psychology and mental health: Social cognition and attitudes, Social influence, Psychological disorders, Treatment and therapy
